subject.title: [Bug]: Stale exec-approvals.json.lock permanently fail-closes exec to security=deny — stale owner detected but never reclaimed

question: Should OpenClaw add a race-safe stale-lock recovery mechanism for exec approvals, or keep fail-closed runtime behavior and provide an explicit supported recovery path?
rationale: Current code intentionally rejects stale-lock reclamation to avoid a cross-process path-replacement race, so choosing between a stronger lock protocol and an operator recovery workflow is a security/availability tradeoff rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Design safe reclamation
options.body: Replace the current stale-lock handling only with a protocol that proves ownership/replacement safety across processes, then cover both sync and async approvals access.

options.title: Add supported recovery
options.body: Keep runtime fail-closed and add a visible Doctor or gateway recovery path that diagnoses the stale lock and removes it under an explicitly reviewed safety contract.

options.title: Keep current behavior
options.body: Preserve fail-closed handling without recovery, accepting manual lock removal as the operational response.

recommendation.title: Design safe reclamation
recommendation.body: Replace the current stale-lock handling only with a protocol that proves ownership/replacement safety across processes, then cover both sync and async approvals access.

likelyOwner.reason: The central exec-approvals implementation history and the shared locking boundary point to this contributor as the strongest available routing candidate.
